findings.location: src/http/process-projection.ts (readEvents: ORDER BY occurred_at ASC LIMIT 200; listInstanceProjections)
findings.issue: Pre-existing (diff is 104/0 additive — cap untouched): the LIST projection fetches the OLDEST 200 process.started rows. A tenant with >200 instances loses visibility of NEWER processes for everyone — not an effect of the new filter. T-0722 does not worsen it (the filter only removes rows the actor was never entitled to see; no entitled, in-window instance is dropped), but the security fix makes the cap more visible (honest-empty instead of 200 leaked rows). No pagination/count field exists to desync (endpoint returns only instances[]; instances.length computed AFTER the filter).
findings.suggestion: Follow-up (out of scope, not blocking): newest-first ordering + explicit pagination / show-all for the LIST projection. Documented in ADR T-0722 §2.3(b).

findings.issue: Documented deferral (phase-1/2 scope, symmetric with DETAIL T-0721): record-less instances (explicit-launch /api/processes/start, no on_create record binding) are NOT narrowed — kept unconditionally. Legitimate, not a leak: record_id is written in the starter's tenant tx; null means no source-record binding ever existed (never a lost link to a foreign record), and the instance is already tenant-scoped by the projection fold.
findings.suggestion: Phase-3 (process-definition-scoped read grant) closes it; out of scope for T-0714 option (c) phases 1-2.
